newsitem.title: JAPAN: MOF says to cut deficit bond issues from '98/99.
newsitem.headline: MOF says to cut deficit bond issues from '98/99.

text.p: Japan plans to cut the amount of deficit-financing bonds it issues by 1.25 trillion yen a year starting with the 1998/99 fiscal year, Japanese Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka told reporters on Tuesday.

Mitsuzuka said in order to achieve the government's target of reducing state debt to three percent of annual gross domestic product (GDP) by 2003, annual issues of deficit-financing bonds must be cut by 1.25 trillion yen.
The government earlier pledged to speed up its plans on fiscal reform, including a plan to stop issues of deficit-financing bonds by 2003. It had originally planned to reach the two targets by 2005.
"In order to put a stop to issues of deficit-financing bonds, we need to cut the issue amount by 1.25 trillion yen a year, instead of the original plan of one trillion yen," Mitsuzuka said.
The finance minister also said the government will consider cutting the budget allocated for public works.
Under its fiscal reform plans, the government will make substantial cuts on spending on long-term projects, including public works.
Asked whether the reform measures will constrict economic growth, Mitsuzuka said the measures will work to invigorate the economy, not hinder it.
The government will now look into details of possible spending cuts and plans to come up with a draft for a bill on fiscal reform by the middle of May, he added.
